CSX.thesis_one_line: Eastern US freight railroad with improving margins and volume, but priced for faster growth than its record or my base case supports.
kill_criteria: GAAP operating margin below 34.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 38.3%, H1'26 37.2%; FY25 32.1%).
Consolidated net debt (current maturities + long-term debt less cash and short-term investments) / TTM (operating income + D&A) above 3.2x (now ~2.6x).
Total carload volume down year over year for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 +6%, H1'26 +4%).
TTM operating cash flow less property additions below $2.0bn (now ~$2.8bn) or 2026 capex guidance raised above $2.6bn.
CSX signs a definitive agreement to acquire or merge with another Class I railroad at consideration above $10bn, or an STB decision materially adverse to CSX's interchange position.
key_adverse_facts: Price implies ~9.5% 10-year FCF growth vs ~7% base and 5.2% delivered 5y (V1).
Q2 revenue +10% is inflated by fuel surcharge ($410m vs $222m); fuel lag was -$54m and fuel expense +$177m.
Unresolved industry consolidation (UNP/NS merger needs STB approval); Q2 MD&A cites advisory expenses related to potential industry consolidation.
Current maturities of debt rose to $1,702m from $708m; buybacks partly debt-funded; CTO separated 2026-05-14.
data_conflicts: V1 implied growth 13.9% and base -8.2% vs my FCF reverse DCF 9.5% implied and +2.7% base; different growth frames.
Yahoo TTM FCF $1.95bn vs my OCF less property additions ~$2.8bn (company FCF definition includes disposals).
CSX.confidence_in_thesis: medium: primary 10-Q/8-K data clear; company gives no earnings guidance and merger outcome is open

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Both say the price exceeds what the business has delivered; V1's -8.2% base uses a 13.9% implied-growth frame, while my FCF reverse DCF implies 9.5% vs a ~7% base (base return +2.7%/yr), so I am less negative but still WATCH. [DV11 2026-10-06: at a consistent 10.17% cost of equity (5.17% + 1.207 x 4.14%) the FCF reverse DCF implies 13.4%, close to V1's 13.9%; implied_vs_base stays above; the 7% base is reached only near $29 a share.]

CSX.scenario_basis: Start EPS $2.00 (2026E), growth 0/7/12%, exit P/E 15/20/24x, dividend $0.56/share/yr.

UHS.thesis_one_line: Big US hospital and mental-health operator priced like earnings will stop growing, but about half its profit depends on Medicaid programs Congress is trimming.
kill_criteria: Full-year Adjusted EPS guidance midpoint cut again below $21.50 (now $22.97), or actual FY2026 adjusted EPS below $21.50.
Aggregate net benefit from Provider Tax Programs (10-Q Medicaid table) projected below $1.2bn for a fiscal year (now $1,481m for 2026), or a state directed-payment program is denied by CMS.
Consolidated net debt (carrying debt less cash) / Adjusted EBITDA net of NCI above 3.0x (now ~1.8x pre-Talkspace).
Same-facility acute and behavioral adjusted admissions both negative for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: +2.9% and +0.5%).
A professional-liability or government settlement/judgment against UHS of Delaware above $250m becomes final and enforceable.
key_adverse_facts: 2026 guidance cut on 2026-07-27: Adjusted EPS $22.28-23.65 vs prior $22.64-24.52; H2 implied ~$11.37 vs H1 $11.60.
Projected 2026 Medicaid provider-tax program net benefit $1,481m pre-tax, ~56% of guided Adjusted EBITDA; OBBBA reduces supplemental payments.
Q2'26 EPS includes +$72m net pre-tax items (incl. $100m Florida prior-period benefit); underlying margin 11.1% vs 11.7%.
Behavioral-health litigation: Cumberland ~43 further plaintiffs; Nevada $500m punitive verdict vacated, retrial expected 2028; +$28m malpractice reserve in Q2.
Aug 2026 refinancing of 1.65% notes with 5.5%/6.0% notes plus Talkspace acquisition raises interest cost and debt.
data_conflicts: Triage said EPS declining; filings show TTM GAAP EPS $24.50 and FY25 adjusted $21.74 (up), though 2026 guidance was cut.
Yahoo shares outstanding 51.7m (class B only) vs ~58.9m implied/59.9m diluted; I used ~58.9m.
Yahoo FCF $498m vs my OCF less capex ~$845m.
UHS.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cheap on any earnings measure, but the supplemental-payment exposure and litigation limit conviction; Q3 date is an estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for UHS, so nothing to reconcile; my reverse DCF (about -0.2% implied FCF CAGR) is below the +5% base, supporting 'cheap' with a named Medicaid reservation.

UHS.scenario_basis: Start underlying EPS $22.00 (guide mid $22.97 less ~$1.3 prior-period item), growth -8/+5/+9%, exit P/E 6/8.5/10.5x, dividend $0.80/share/yr.

KO.thesis_one_line: World's largest soft-drink brand owner raising guidance steadily, but its share price already assumes near-flawless growth for a decade.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue (non-GAAP) growth below 3% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 +6%, Q1'26 +10% incl. six extra days).
Global unit case volume growth negative for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 +5%, Q1'26 +3%).
Full-year comparable EPS growth guidance cut below 7% (currently 9% to 10%, 7% to 8% currency neutral ex-M&A).
Consolidated net debt (carrying debt less cash, short-term investments and marketable securities) / (TTM operating income + D&A) above 2.5x (now ~1.7x).
An unfavourable appellate ruling in the IRS transfer pricing case adding more than $1.0bn of tax and interest beyond the $6.0bn deposit.
key_adverse_facts: Price 26.7-26.9x 2026 guided comparable EPS; FCF yield ~3.3% on $12.4bn guide; implied FCF CAGR ~6.5% vs ~6% base.
About 3 points of 2026 EPS growth is currency tailwind; ~2 of the ~3 points of the latest raise are real (currency-neutral 7-8% vs prior 6-7%).
fairlife ransomware (8-K 2026-07-16): US production suspended, majority resumed per 10-Q; company says not reasonably likely material.
IRS transfer-pricing case: $6.0bn deposit paid; outcome on appeal pending.
Net debt ~$27.2bn consolidated; $5.4bn assets held for sale (Africa bottling) closing by end-2026.
data_conflicts: Triage FCF yield 1.4% reflects FY25 fairlife milestone payment (~$6.1bn, derived); normalised 2026 guide FCF $12.4bn = ~3.3% yield.
GAAP EPS $1.03 vs comparable $0.97 in Q2'26: $320m securities gain and Africa impairment reversal.
KO.confidence_in_thesis: high on business quality, medium on valuation: guidance is raised three releases in a row but date for Q3 is an estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for KO, so nothing to reconcile; my reverse DCF implies ~6.5% FCF growth vs ~6% base, a marginal premium, hence WATCH rather than INCLUDE.

KO.scenario_basis: Start 2026E comparable EPS $3.285, growth 3/7.5/9.5%, exit P/E 21/25/27x, dividend $2.12/share/yr.
